experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the spectacular wildebeest migration in the Maasai Mara National Reserve. Join guided game drives to observe millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles crossing the Mara River, along with predators like lions, cheetahs, and leopards in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Mount Kilimanjaro Backdrop
experiences.description: Explore Amboseli National Park, home to some of Africa's largest elephant herds. Enjoy breathtaking views of Mount Kilimanjaro as a backdrop while observing elephants, buffalo, and diverse birdlife on guided game drives across the open savannah plains.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Safari
experiences.description: Visit Lake Nakuru National Park, famous for its stunning flocks of pink flamingos coating the alkaline lake shores. The park is also a critical sanctuary for both black and white rhinos, offering rare rhino tracking experiences alongside sightings of lions, leopards, and Rothschild giraffes.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Chimpanzee Sanctuary Visit
experiences.description: Explore Ol Pejeta Conservancy, East Africa's largest black rhino sanctuary and home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth. Visit the Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary, take guided bush walks, and enjoy night game drives to spot nocturnal wildlife rarely seen on standard safaris.

experiences.name: Kakamega Rainforest Nature Walk & Birdwatching
experiences.description: Trek through Kakamega Forest, Kenya's only tropical rainforest and a biodiversity hotspot. Guided nature walks reveal rare primates including De Brazza's monkeys and red-tailed monkeys, over 330 bird species, giant African millipedes, and ancient hardwood trees in a lush, untouched ecosystem.
experiences.location: Kakamega Forest National Reserve, Kakamega County

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange shared shuttle or budget matatu transfer toward Narok. The journey to Maasai Mara takes approximately 5-6 hours. Enjoy the scenic drive through the Great Rift Valley escarpment and rolling savannah landscapes. Stop at a roadside viewpoint near Narok town for photos.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your boutique stay in Maasai Mara National Reserve. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodation. Take a short walk around the lodge grounds at dusk to spot birds and small wildlife. Attend any welcome briefing offered by the lodge about park rules, safety, and upcoming game drive schedules.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or during the flight - grab a snack at the airport if needed
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch or grab a quick affordable bite at a roadside kiosk near Narok town (chapati, samosa, or mandazi for under KES 200)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge or nearby budget camp dining area - opt for the set menu which typically includes ugali, sukuma wiki, and stewed meat or beans (KES 800-1200)

day_by_day.notes: Book your shared shuttle in advance to save costs. Carry KES cash as ATMs are scarce near the Mara. Bring a light jacket for the evening as temperatures can drop to 15°C after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn for an early morning game drive departing at 06:00 into the Maasai Mara National Reserve. July is peak Great Migration season - witness massive wildebeest and zebra herds moving across the plains. Look for the Big Five: lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino. A shared game drive vehicle with other lodge guests keeps costs down (KES 3,000-5,000 per person for a half-day shared drive).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge by 10:00 for a late breakfast. Rest during the hottest part of the day. At 15:00, head out for an afternoon game drive focusing on the Mara River crossing points where wildebeest attempt dramatic river crossings with Nile crocodiles waiting below. This is one of the greatest wildlife spectacles on Earth.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp at sunset around 18:30. Enjoy sundowners on the lodge terrace watching the golden savannah light. Share stories with fellow travelers about the day's wildlife sightings. Stargaze from the camp grounds - light pollution is minimal and the Milky Way is often visible.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast included or opt for budget porridge and eggs at the camp kitchen (KES 400-600)
meals.lunch: Simple packed lunch or light meal at the lodge - request a budget picnic box (KES 500-700) to eat in the field
meals.dinner: Communal campfire dinner at the lodge - traditional Kenyan stew with ugali and vegetables (KES 900-1,300)

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, olive, brown) for game drives. Bring binoculars if possible. Sunscreen, a hat, and a camera with a zoom lens are essential. The Mara River crossings are unpredictable - patience is key.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning balloon safari alternative: if budget allows, a hot air balloon ride over the Mara at sunrise is a once-in-a-lifetime experience (USD 450-500, splurge option). Budget alternative: arrange a guided walking safari with a Maasai guide around the lodge perimeter and nearby bush for KES 1,500-2,000 per person. Learn to track animals on foot, identify bird species, and understand local plant medicinal uses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Maasai village (manyatta) near the reserve boundary. Engage with community members, learn about traditional Maasai culture, beadwork, and cattle herding practices. Purchase handmade beaded jewelry and crafts directly from artisans to support the community (budget KES 500-1,500 for souvenirs). This cultural exchange is typically arranged through the lodge for KES 1,000-1,500 per person.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Maasai dance and music performance at the village or lodge grounds. Watch the adumu jumping dance performed by Maasai warriors. Return to camp for dinner and an early night to prepare for another dawn game drive tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the lodge before the walking safari - tea, bread, and fruit (KES 300-500)
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Maasai village or back at the lodge - try traditional Maasai tea (chai ya maziwa) with milk and spices (KES 400-700)
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner - nyama choma (grilled goat meat) with kachumbari salad and ugali, a Kenyan classic (KES 1,000-1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Ask permission before photographing Maasai community members. Bring small gifts like pens or notebooks for village children. The walking safari requires closed-toe shoes and long trousers for protection against thorns and insects.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day game drive departing at 06:00 focusing on the northern Mara Triangle, which is managed by the Mara Conservancy and tends to be less crowded than the main reserve. Look for cheetah on open plains, hyena dens, and vast elephant herds. The Mara Triangle offers some of the best big cat sightings in Africa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the full-day game drive with a picnic lunch in the bush near a waterhole. Observe wildlife coming to drink throughout the afternoon. Look for hippo pods in the Mara River and crocodiles basking on the banks. Spot hundreds of bird species including lilac-breasted rollers, secretary birds, and fish eagles.
day_by_day.evening: Return to lodge by 18:30. Relax with a cold Tusker beer or fresh passion fruit juice at the camp bar. Write in a travel journal or review the day's wildlife photographs. Join other guests for a communal evening sharing the day's highlights.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast box from the lodge to eat in the vehicle (KES 400-600)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the bush - sandwiches, fruit, and juice prepared by the lodge kitchen (KES 600-800, request budget option)
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner - bean stew with chapati and steamed vegetables, a filling budget-friendly option (KES 800-1,100)

day_by_day.notes: A full-day shared game drive costs approximately KES 5,000-7,000 per person including park fees. Always carry at least 2 liters of water per person. Do not exit the vehicle in the reserve without a licensed guide.

day_by_day.morning: Morning game drive with a specific focus on birdwatching - the Maasai Mara hosts over 450 bird species. Hire a specialist birding guide through the lodge for a more detailed experience (KES 2,000-3,000 for a half-day). Spot ostriches, kori bustards, ground hornbills, and various vulture species. The open grasslands are perfect for raptors including martial eagles and bateleurs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and relaxation at the lodge during peak afternoon heat. Use this time to review wildlife photos, read, or take a nap. At 16:00, take a self-guided nature walk around the lodge's immediate grounds with a checklist of common birds and plants provided by the lodge. Photograph insects, butterflies, and small reptiles in the lodge garden.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset game drive departing at 17:00 for golden hour photography. The warm evening light creates stunning conditions for wildlife photography. Look for nocturnal animals beginning their activity - aardvarks, genets, and bush babies may be spotted as darkness falls. Return by 19:00.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast - scrambled eggs, toast, fresh fruit, and Kenyan tea (KES 500-700)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the lodge - avocado on toast or vegetable soup (Kenya produces excellent avocados) (KES 400-600)
meals.dinner: Outdoor campfire dinner under the stars - grilled fish with rice and coconut bean soup (KES 900-1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Download a birding app such as Merlin Bird ID before the trip to help identify species. The afternoon rest period is important for conserving energy during the warm midday hours of 25°C+.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive focusing on predator activity. Lions and leopards are most active at dawn. Ask your guide to search specific areas known for big cat sightings. Witness a potential hunt or feeding scene - raw and powerful nature at its finest. The Mara is home to one of the highest lion densities in Africa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Maasai Mara toward Lake Nakuru National Park via shared transport or budget shuttle (approximately 4-5 hours, KES 1,500-2,500). En route, stop at the Great Rift Valley viewpoint near Naivasha for panoramic photos. Arrive at Lake Nakuru and check into a budget guesthouse or campsite outside the park gates (KES 1,500-3,000 per night).
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Lake Nakuru accommodation. Take an evening stroll around the town of Nakuru to experience local Kenyan urban life. Visit a local market to stock up on fresh fruit, snacks, and water at very affordable prices. Enjoy dinner at a local restaurant in Nakuru town.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast in the Mara - eat well before the long transfer (KES 500-700)
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop at a local hotel in Naivasha town - pilau rice with chicken or beef (KES 300-500, excellent value)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant in Nakuru town - try mukimo (mashed potatoes with peas and corn) with stewed beef, a Central Kenya specialty (KES 400-700)

day_by_day.notes: Book shared transport the day before to secure a seat. Keep valuables secure during town exploration in Nakuru. The budget guesthouse should be booked in advance - options include Midland Hotel or similar budget properties near the park.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day game drive in Lake Nakuru National Park. The park is famous for its flamingo populations on the alkaline lake shores - in July you may see tens of thousands of lesser and greater flamingoes creating a stunning pink carpet. The park also protects both black and white rhinos, making it one of the best rhino sanctuaries in East Africa. Park entry fee: KES 5,285 for non-residents or KES 600 for East African residents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Lake Nakuru NP. Visit Baboon Cliff and Lion Hill for elevated panoramic views over the lake and surrounding escarpment. Spot Rothschild giraffes, waterbuck, and large buffalo herds. The park is compact and easily covered in a full day. Look for the resident leopards resting in acacia trees along the lake's western shore.
day_by_day.evening: Exit the park by 18:00. Return to Nakuru town for the evening. Visit the lively Nakuru town center and experience local nightlife at a budget-friendly bar or restaurant. Try fresh sugarcane juice from street vendors (KES 30-50).

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast - tea, bread with Blue Band margarine, and a boiled egg (KES 200-400)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch inside the park - pack food from town the night before to save money (bread, fruit, juice, KES 300-500 total)
meals.dinner: Local Nakuru restaurant - tilapia fish with ugali and sukuma wiki, a classic Kenyan lakeside meal (KES 500-800)

day_by_day.notes: Hire a shared taxi/tuk-tuk to the park gate from town (KES 200-300). A self-drive rental or shared tour vehicle is needed inside the park. Budget tour operators in Nakuru offer shared game drives for KES 2,000-3,500 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to Lake Elementaita, a smaller Rift Valley soda lake located between Nakuru and Naivasha (accessible by matatu, KES 100-150). This UNESCO World Heritage Site is a flamingo breeding ground and bird sanctuary. Walk along the lake shore freely without park fees for excellent birdwatching and photography. Spot pelicans, herons, and thousands of flamingoes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Hell's Gate National Park near Naivasha (matatu from Nakuru via Naivasha, total KES 300-500). Hell's Gate is unique as visitors can walk and cycle through the park without a vehicle, making it one of Kenya's most budget-friendly parks (entry KES 3,530 non-residents or KES 215 residents). Rent a bicycle at the gate (KES 500-800) and cycle through dramatic gorge landscapes with zebras, giraffes, and warthogs roaming freely alongside you.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Hell's Gate Gorge on foot - a narrow volcanic gorge with hot springs and geothermal steam vents. The scenery inspired Disney's The Lion King film. Exit the park by 18:00 and find budget accommodation in Naivasha town (KES 1,000-2,500 per night at local guesthouses).

meals.breakfast: Street breakfast in Nakuru before departure - mandazi (fried doughnuts) and chai (KES 100-150)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch to eat while cycling in Hell's Gate - buy supplies at Naivasha market (KES 300-500)
meals.dinner: Naivasha town local restaurant - githeri (corn and bean stew) with chapati, hearty and very affordable (KES 300-500)

day_by_day.notes: Hell's Gate is one of Africa's only parks where you can walk and cycle freely among wildlife - an extraordinary budget experience. Carry enough water as it can be warm. The gorge walk takes 2-3 hours and involves some scrambling over rocks.

day_by_day.morning: Morning boat trip on Lake Naivasha - one of Kenya's freshwater Rift Valley lakes. Budget boat rides can be arranged at the public boat launch for KES 500-1,000 per person for a 1-hour trip. Spot hippos lazing in the water, fish eagles swooping for prey, and hundreds of waterbirds including African jacanas, cormorants, and kingfishers. Crescent Island (accessible by boat) offers a free-walking wildlife experience with giraffes and zebras.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Crescent Island Game Sanctuary on Lake Naivasha (boat transfer + entry approximately KES 2,000-2,500 total). Walk freely among giraffes, zebras, wildebeest, and antelopes on this small island peninsula - no fences, no vehicles, just you and the wildlife. The views across the lake to Mount Longonot volcano are spectacular. Spend 2-3 hours exploring before returning by boat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Naivasha town. Begin preparing for the return journey to Nairobi tomorrow. Pack and organize luggage. Enjoy a final Rift Valley evening watching the sunset over the lake from a viewpoint. Treat yourself to a slightly better dinner to celebrate the end of a remarkable safari adventure.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast - porridge with milk and sugar, toast, and Kenyan tea (KES 200-400)
meals.lunch: Lakeside lunch at a budget restaurant near the boat launch - fried tilapia with chips and salad (KES 600-900)
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at a mid-range local restaurant in Naivasha - nyama choma platter with kachumbari and cold Tusker beer (KES 1,200-1,800)

day_by_day.notes: Negotiate boat prices firmly but fairly - always agree on the price before boarding. Wear a life jacket during boat trips. Crescent Island is best visited in the morning when animals are most active near the shoreline.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Rift Valley. Wake early for one last sunrise walk along Lake Naivasha shores (free). Watch the morning mist lift over the water and enjoy the peaceful sounds of Africa waking up - hippos grunting, fish eagles calling, and papyrus reeds rustling. Take final photos and soak in the atmosphere. Pack up and check out of accommodation by 09:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a matatu or shared shuttle from Naivasha to Nairobi (approximately 1.5-2 hours, KES 200-400). Arrive in Nairobi with time to explore the city center. Visit the Nairobi National Museum (KES 1,200 entry) for an overview of Kenyan history, culture, and natural history. Alternatively, visit the Karen Blixen Museum (KES 1,200) for literary and colonial history. Stop at Maasai Market (held at various Nairobi locations on rotating days) for last-minute souvenir shopping - negotiate prices confidently.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for departure. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Spend remaining Kenyan shillings on airport snacks or duty-free Kenyan coffee and tea to take home. Reflect on an incredible 10 days of wildlife, culture, and natural wonders across Kenya's most spectacular landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Final Kenyan breakfast before departure - chapati with eggs and chai at a local café in Naivasha (KES 200-350)
meals.lunch: Quick affordable lunch in Nairobi city center - Java House or a local restaurant offering rice and stew (KES 500-800)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or pack snacks from Nairobi for the flight (budget KES 500-1,000 for airport food)

day_by_day.notes: Keep airport transfer time in mind - Nairobi traffic can be severe, especially in the afternoon. Allow extra time. Exchange any remaining KES back to your home currency at the airport or use it for final purchases. Kenya imposes an airport departure tax included in most international tickets.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from Nairobi to Maasai Mara National Reserve (approximately 5–6 hours by road or 45 minutes by charter flight). Enjoy the scenic drive through the Great Rift Valley escarpment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at your boutique stay in Maasai Mara National Reserve. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a welcome briefing from your lodge naturalist. Take a short guided walk around the lodge perimeter to spot resident birds and small wildlife.
day_by_day.evening: Settle in with a sundowner drink on the lodge veranda as the African sun sets over the savannah. Attend a brief orientation session about the Mara ecosystem and what to expect over the coming days.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or light snack at Nairobi airport
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or light meal at a roadside stop en route to the Mara (budget ~$10–15)
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the boutique lodge's dining area — enjoy a set Kenyan bush dinner with nyama choma (roasted meat), ugali, and sukuma wiki (~$25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport transfer in advance. If budget allows, a 45-minute charter flight from Wilson Airport to Mara airstrips saves significant travel time. Pack a light jacket for the cool Mara evenings (temperatures can drop to 14–16°C after sunset).

day_by_day.morning: Early morning full-day Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari game drive departing at 06:00. Head to the Mara River crossing points to witness the dramatic wildebeest and zebra migration crossings — July is peak season. Look for the Big Five along the way: lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the game drive through the open plains. Stop at a scenic viewpoint for a packed bush lunch. Spot cheetahs, giraffes, hippos in the Mara River, and vast herds of wildebeest stretching to the horizon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge by 18:30. Enjoy hot showers and relax around the campfire. Optional stargazing session with a lodge guide identifying Southern Hemisphere constellations.

meals.breakfast: Early bush breakfast at the lodge before departure — eggs, toast, fresh fruit, and Kenyan tea/coffee (~included or $8–12)
meals.lunch: Packed bush picnic lunch provided by the lodge or guide service, enjoyed in the field (~$12–18)
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at the lodge restaurant — grilled tilapia or beef stew with local vegetables and chapati (~$25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-coloured clothing (khaki, olive, brown) for game drives. Bring sunscreen, a hat, binoculars, and a camera with a zoom lens. The Great Migration river crossings are unpredictable — patience is key. Book migration safari through your lodge or a reputable operator (~$80–120 per person for a full-day drive).

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hot-air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara at 06:00 (optional but highly recommended). Float silently over the golden savannah watching wildlife from above — lions on kills, elephant herds, and the endless wildebeest migration. A truly unforgettable experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing and a champagne bush breakfast, return to the lodge and rest. In the afternoon, join a guided Maasai cultural village visit near the reserve boundary. Learn about Maasai traditions, beadwork, warrior jumping dances, and their coexistence with wildlife.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset game drive from 16:00–18:30, focusing on predator activity during the golden hour. Lions and leopards are most active at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Champagne bush breakfast included with the balloon safari on the open plains (~included in balloon package)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the lodge — sandwiches, salads, and fresh juice (~$12–18)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge — try Kenyan lamb stew (nyama ya kondoo) with pilau rice and kachumbari salad (~$25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hot-air balloon safaris cost approximately $450–500 per person and must be booked well in advance. This is a once-in-a-lifetime experience worth budgeting for. The Maasai village visit typically costs $20–30 per person — ensure your guide uses a community-run, ethical village.

day_by_day.morning: Morning game drive focused on the Mara Triangle (western section of the reserve), known for fewer crowds and exceptional wildlife density. Look for leopards in riverine forests along the Mara River and large lion prides on the open plains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to lodge for lunch and a midday rest during the hottest part of the day. Participate in an optional guided nature walk with a Maasai ranger around the lodge's private conservancy — spot birds, insects, and plant life up close on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Night game drive (if permitted by your lodge/conservancy) to spot nocturnal wildlife — servals, genets, bush babies, and hyenas. Alternatively, enjoy a bush dinner under the stars with a bonfire.

meals.breakfast: Full English-style bush breakfast at the lodge — eggs, sausages, beans, toast, and fresh fruit (~included or $8–12)
meals.lunch: Lodge buffet lunch — selection of Kenyan salads, grilled meats, and fresh bread (~$15–20)
meals.dinner: Bush dinner under the stars (if offered by lodge) or dining room — grilled chicken with coconut rice and mango salsa (~$25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Mara Triangle is managed by the Mara Conservancy and has separate entry fees (~$80 per vehicle). Night drives are only permitted in private conservancies bordering the reserve, not inside the national reserve itself. Confirm availability with your lodge.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Maasai Mara early and transfer to Lake Nakuru National Park (approximately 3.5–4 hours by road via Narok and Nakuru town). En route, stop at the Great Rift Valley viewpoint for panoramic photographs of the valley floor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Lake Nakuru and begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo and Rhino Safari. The alkaline lake is famous for thousands of pink flamingos lining its shores. Spot white rhinos grazing on the lakeshore — Lake Nakuru is a rhino sanctuary. Look for Rothschild's giraffes, waterbuck, and African fish eagles.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a mid-range lodge or tented camp near Lake Nakuru (e.g., Lake Nakuru Sopa Lodge or similar). Enjoy the elevated views over the lake at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Maasai Mara lodge before departure (~included)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch enjoyed at a picnic site inside Lake Nakuru National Park (~$12–18)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lake Nakuru lodge — buffet-style with Kenyan and continental options including fresh lake fish (~$20–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru National Park entry fees are approximately $60 per adult per day. The flamingo population varies seasonally but July typically offers good sightings. Book mid-range accommodation near the park in advance — options range from $80–150 per night. The drive from Mara to Nakuru passes through scenic highland farmland.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning game drive inside Lake Nakuru National Park. Focus on the southern lakeshore for flamingo and pelican concentrations. Visit the baboon cliff viewpoint for sweeping views over the entire lake. Look for lions that frequently den in the rocky escarpments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Lake Nakuru and drive north to Ol Pejeta Conservancy (approximately 2.5 hours via Nakuru–Nyahururu–Nanyuki road). Check in to a mid-range camp inside or adjacent to Ol Pejeta Conservancy.
day_by_day.evening: Evening sundowner game drive inside Ol Pejeta Conservancy. Spot the famous northern white rhinos (Sudan's descendants) and black rhinos in their natural habitat. The conservancy is also home to lions, elephants, and cheetahs.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Lake Nakuru lodge before departure (~included or $10–15)
meals.lunch: Stop in Nyahururu town for lunch at a local restaurant — try pilau rice with beef or chicken stew, a filling and authentic Kenyan meal (~$5–10)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ol Pejeta camp or lodge — enjoy a hearty bush dinner with campfire ambiance (~$25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ol Pejeta Conservancy entry fees are approximately $90 per adult per day. The conservancy is the only place in East Africa where you can see the last two northern white rhinos (Najin and Fatu). Photography of these animals is a profound and moving experience. Mid-range accommodation options include Sweetwaters Serena Camp (~$150–200 per night).

day_by_day.morning: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Chimpanzee Sanctuary Visit. This is East Africa's only chimpanzee sanctuary, housing rescued chimps from across Central and West Africa. Join a guided tour to observe the chimps at close range in their forested enclosures — an extraordinary and educational experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive through Ol Pejeta's vast open plains. With Mount Kenya visible on clear days, this is one of Kenya's most scenic conservancies. Look for the 'Sweetwaters' resident lion pride, large elephant herds, and endangered black rhinos.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp for a relaxed evening. Optional visit to the conservancy's information centre to learn about rhino conservation efforts and anti-poaching initiatives. Bonfire and storytelling session with Maasai and Samburu rangers.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the camp — fresh fruit, eggs, and Kenyan tea (~included or $10–12)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the field or at the conservancy's visitor centre café (~$12–18)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the camp — grilled game meat (if available) or beef tenderloin with roasted vegetables and ugali (~$25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The chimpanzee sanctuary visit costs approximately $60–80 per person and should be booked in advance through Ol Pejeta. Morning feeding sessions (around 09:00 and 15:00) offer the best viewing opportunities. Mount Kenya is most visible in the early morning before clouds build — bring a telephoto lens for stunning mountain backdrop shots.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Ol Pejeta Conservancy and drive west to Kakamega Forest (approximately 4–5 hours via Nakuru and Eldoret). The journey passes through Kenya's fertile highland tea and maize farming regions — a beautiful contrast to the savannah.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Kakamega Forest and check in to a mid-range guesthouse or eco-lodge (e.g., Rondo Retreat Centre or Udo's Bandas). Begin the Kakamega Rainforest Nature Walk and Birdwatching experience with a Kenya Wildlife Service guide. Kenya's only tropical rainforest is home to over 330 bird species, 400 butterfly species, and rare primates.
day_by_day.evening: Evening birdwatching walk at dusk — the forest comes alive with the calls of African grey parrots, great blue turacos, and crowned hornbills. Spot de Brazza's monkeys and red-tailed monkeys in the forest canopy.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Ol Pejeta camp before departure (~included)
meals.lunch: Stop in Eldoret for lunch at a local restaurant — try mukimo (mashed potatoes with greens and corn) or a beef chapati wrap (~$5–10)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Kakamega eco-lodge — simple but delicious home-cooked Kenyan meal with fresh vegetables, beans, and ugali (~$15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Kakamega Forest is a UNESCO-recognised biodiversity hotspot and the easternmost remnant of the great Congo rainforest. Guided walks cost approximately $15–25 per person. Wear long sleeves and trousers for forest walks to protect against insects. The forest receives more rainfall than the Mara, so bring a light rain jacket. Accommodation at Rondo Retreat is approximately $60–100 per night.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Kakamega Forest immersion. Early morning birdwatching walk (06:00–09:00) — this is the best time to spot rare species including the Chapin's flycatcher, Turner's eremomela, and the striking African crowned eagle. A specialist birding guide is highly recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided forest hike to the Isiukhu Falls and Lirhanda Hill viewpoint. The trail winds through ancient hardwood trees, ferns, and orchids. Learn about traditional medicinal plants used by the Luhya community from your forest guide. Spot forest elephants, bushbuck, and giant African land snails.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the eco-lodge for a relaxed final evening in the forest. Participate in an optional cultural evening with local Luhya community members — traditional music, dance, and craft demonstration.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before birdwatching — fresh fruit, porridge, and Kenyan tea at the lodge (~$8–12)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch in the forest or at Isiukhu Falls picnic area (~$10–15)
meals.dinner: Farewell forest dinner at the lodge — grilled tilapia from Lake Victoria (nearby) with coconut rice and fresh salad (~$15–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: July is an excellent month for Kakamega birdwatching as many resident species are actively breeding. The forest can be muddy after rain — wear sturdy waterproof hiking boots. A full-day forest experience with multiple guides costs approximately $30–50 per person. Consider purchasing locally made crafts and honey from community members to support conservation livelihoods.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning sunrise walk in Kakamega Forest — a peaceful farewell to Kenya's wildlife. Pack up and check out of the eco-lodge. Begin the drive back to Nairobi (approximately 5–6 hours via Kisumu and Nakuru, or 6–7 hours via Eldoret and the Rift Valley).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Nairobi. If time permits before your departure flight, visit the Giraffe Centre in Karen (home to the endangered Rothschild's giraffe) or the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust Elephant Orphanage for a final wildlife encounter in the capital. Both are excellent and affordable.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for departure. Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security. Reflect on an extraordinary 10 days of Kenya's finest wildlife, landscapes, and culture.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Kakamega lodge — enjoy a leisurely Kenyan breakfast before the long drive (~included or $8–12)
meals.lunch: Stop in Nakuru or Naivasha for lunch at a mid-range restaurant — try nyama choma with chips and kachumbari for a classic Kenyan farewell meal (~$10–18)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Nairobi restaurant near the airport if time allows — try Carnivore Restaurant for a classic Kenyan game meat experience, or a lighter meal at Java House (~$15–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Giraffe Centre is open 09:00–17:00 and costs approximately $15 per adult. The David Sheldrick Elephant Orphanage public visiting hours are 11:00–12:00 daily ($7 per person). Both are in the Karen/Langata suburb, about 20–25 minutes from the city centre and 30–40 minutes from JKIA. Allow ample buffer time for Nairobi traffic, which can be severe during afternoon rush hours. Ensure all wildlife souvenirs comply with CITES regulations — avoid any ivory, coral, or animal skin products.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Kenya Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the spectacular wildebeest migration in the Maasai Mara National Reserve. Join guided game drives to observe millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles crossing the Mara River, along with predators like lions, cheetahs, and leopards in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Mount Kilimanjaro Backdrop
experiences.description: Explore Amboseli National Park, home to some of Africa's largest elephant herds. Enjoy breathtaking views of Mount Kilimanjaro as a backdrop while observing elephants, buffalo, and diverse birdlife on guided game drives across the open savannah plains.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Safari
experiences.description: Visit Lake Nakuru National Park, famous for its stunning flocks of pink flamingos coating the alkaline lake shores. The park is also a critical sanctuary for both black and white rhinos, offering rare rhino tracking experiences alongside sightings of lions, leopards, and Rothschild giraffes.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Chimpanzee Sanctuary Visit
experiences.description: Explore Ol Pejeta Conservancy, East Africa's largest black rhino sanctuary and home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth. Visit the Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary, take guided bush walks, and enjoy night game drives to spot nocturnal wildlife rarely seen on standard safaris.

experiences.name: Kakamega Rainforest Nature Walk & Birdwatching
experiences.description: Trek through Kakamega Forest, Kenya's only tropical rainforest and a biodiversity hotspot. Guided nature walks reveal rare primates including De Brazza's monkeys and red-tailed monkeys, over 330 bird species, giant African millipedes, and ancient hardwood trees in a lush, untouched ecosystem.
experiences.location: Kakamega Forest National Reserve, Kakamega County

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to meet you at the airport with a welcome refreshment pack.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight or luxury road transfer from Nairobi to Maasai Mara National Reserve (approx. 45 min by air or 5–6 hrs by road). Scenic aerial views of the Rift Valley en route. Arrive at boutique lodge, enjoy a personal welcome with chilled towels, fresh juices, and a lodge orientation tour.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your luxury suite and unwind on your private veranda overlooking the savannah. Attend a sundowner cocktail session at the lodge's panoramic deck as the sun sets over the Mara plains. Enjoy a welcome dinner under the stars at the lodge's outdoor boma.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport lounge dining prior to arrival
meals.lunch: Gourmet welcome picnic hamper served on arrival at the lodge — artisan sandwiches, local fruits, sparkling water, and Kenyan wines
meals.dinner: Private boma dinner at the lodge featuring Kenyan-inspired cuisine: slow-roasted nyama choma (premium beef), ugali, sukuma wiki, and a curated East African wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Ensure passport and visa documents are readily accessible. A dedicated lodge butler will assist with luggage and room preferences. Light layers recommended for the evening as temperatures can drop to 15–18°C after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Early pre-dawn wake-up for a premium hot air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara at sunrise (approx. 06:00 departure). Drift silently above the golden savannah, spotting lions, elephants, giraffes, and the first herds of the Great Migration from a breathtaking aerial perspective. Flight duration approximately 1 hour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Champagne bush breakfast on the Mara plains following the balloon landing — a classic Kenyan luxury tradition. Return to the lodge for a midday rest, followed by a guided afternoon game drive in a private 4x4 Land Cruiser focusing on big cat sightings — lions, leopards, and cheetahs — in the Mara Triangle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge for a bush bath drawn with rose petals and Mara herbs. Attend a cultural evening with resident Maasai warriors — traditional dances, storytelling, and fire-jumping ceremonies. Retire to a candlelit private dinner in your suite.

meals.breakfast: Champagne bush breakfast on the open plains post-balloon — smoked salmon, scrambled eggs, fresh pastries, tropical fruits, and Moët & Chandon
meals.lunch: Lodge terrace lunch: grilled tilapia, quinoa salad, roasted vegetables, and fresh mango sorbet
meals.dinner: Private in-suite candlelit dinner: pan-seared duck breast, truffle mashed potatoes, sautéed greens, and a premium Kenyan coffee dessert

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon must be pre-booked well in advance — confirm with lodge concierge upon arrival. Weight restrictions apply (typically max 100 kg per passenger). July is peak Great Migration season — exceptional wildlife viewing expected.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari experience. Depart at dawn (05:30) with a private expert guide and tracker for an immersive game drive to witness wildebeest and zebra river crossings at the Mara River — one of the most dramatic wildlife spectacles on Earth. Spend the morning positioned at prime crossing points.
day_by_day.afternoon: Bush lunch served in the field beside the Mara River — a gourmet picnic prepared by lodge chefs. Continue afternoon game drive tracking the migration herds and observing predator-prey interactions. Visit the open grasslands of Governors' Camp area for exceptional big cat density.
day_by_day.evening: Guided night game drive (where permitted) to spot nocturnal species including hyenas, leopards, genets, and bush babies. Return to lodge for a fireside dinner at the main dining area with live acoustic Kenyan music.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast box at the lodge before departure — granola, yogurt, boiled eggs, fresh juice, and Kenyan AA coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet riverside bush picnic: charcuterie board, artisan cheeses, grilled chicken wraps, fresh salads, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Lodge main dining room: slow-cooked Maasai lamb stew, saffron rice, roasted root vegetables, and a decadent chocolate fondant dessert

day_by_day.notes: River crossings are unpredictable — patience is key. Your guide will use radio networks with other guides to locate active crossings. Bring binoculars, a telephoto camera lens, and sunscreen. July crossings are among the most frequent of the year.

day_by_day.morning: Morning guided walking safari with a senior Maasai tracker and armed ranger — explore the bush on foot, learning to track wildlife by footprints, dung, and broken vegetation. Discover the smaller wonders of the Mara: insects, birds, plants, and medicinal herbs used by the Maasai.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a traditional Maasai village (manyatta) for an authentic cultural immersion experience. Meet the village elders, learn about Maasai traditions, beadwork, and cattle herding. Participate in a hands-on beadwork workshop and purchase handcrafted jewelry directly from artisans. Return to the lodge for a spa treatment at the lodge's luxury wellness center.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset game drive along the Mara River banks, watching hippos emerge at dusk and crocodiles basking on the banks. Return for a wine-pairing dinner experience at the lodge featuring South African and Kenyan wines matched to a five-course tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast buffet: fresh tropical fruits, eggs benedict, smoked meats, Kenyan honey, freshly baked breads, and specialty coffees
meals.lunch: Lodge poolside lunch: grilled prawns, avocado salad, sweet potato fries, and passion fruit cheesecake
meals.dinner: Five-course wine-pairing dinner: amuse-bouche, butternut soup, seared tuna tartare, Wagyu beef fillet with Mara herb jus, and a vanilla panna cotta with berry coulis

day_by_day.notes: Walking safaris require closed-toe shoes and neutral-colored clothing. Maasai village visits include a small community donation — lodge concierge will advise on appropriate amounts. Spa treatments should be booked in advance with the lodge wellness team.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Lake Nakuru National Park (approx. 3–4 hour luxury road transfer or 30-minute charter flight from Mara). Arrive for a morning Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Safari — witness thousands of pink flamingos coating the alkaline lake shores in a breathtaking pink carpet display.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Lake Nakuru safari focusing on white and black rhino tracking — Lake Nakuru is one of Kenya's premier rhino sanctuaries. Spot Rothschild's giraffes, African buffaloes, lions, and leopards in the surrounding acacia woodland. Enjoy a luxury lodge lunch at a premium Lake Nakuru property.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to Maasai Mara (charter flight recommended for comfort). Arrive back at the lodge for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a private rooftop dinner under a canopy of stars with a telescope provided for stargazing over the Mara.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast before departure: fresh fruit platter, avocado toast, smoked salmon, and Kenyan tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium Lake Nakuru lodge: grilled Nile perch, roasted vegetables, Kenyan pilau rice, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Private rooftop stargazing dinner at the Mara lodge: lobster bisque, grilled beef tenderloin, truffle risotto, and a dark chocolate tart with Kenyan coffee cream

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru flamingo numbers vary seasonally — July typically offers excellent viewing. Confirm charter flight timings with the lodge the evening before. Rhino tracking may require additional permits arranged by the lodge concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Amboseli National Park (approx. 1-hour charter flight from Mara). Morning Amboseli Elephant Watching safari — explore the park home to some of Africa's largest and most studied elephant herds against the iconic backdrop of snow-capped Mount Kilimanjaro (5,895m). Photograph massive bull elephants in the golden morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive in Amboseli focusing on the diverse ecosystem: lions, cheetahs, zebras, wildebeest, and over 600 bird species. Visit Observation Hill for panoramic views over the swamps and Kilimanjaro. Enjoy sundowners at a premium Amboseli camp.
day_by_day.evening: Return charter flight to Maasai Mara. Lodge welcome-back dinner featuring a special Kenyan fusion menu prepared by the head chef, with a personalized menu card as a keepsake.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast before departure: eggs cooked to order, fresh juices, Kenyan pastries, and AA coffee
meals.lunch: Luxury bush lunch at Amboseli camp: grilled meats, fresh salads, artisan breads, and tropical fruit platters
meals.dinner: Kenyan fusion welcome-back dinner: spiced crab cakes, Swahili-style coconut fish curry, jasmine rice, and a cardamom-infused crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: Mount Kilimanjaro views are clearest in the early morning before clouds build — plan to arrive at Amboseli before 08:00 for the best photographic conditions. Amboseli elephants are habituated to vehicles, allowing exceptionally close encounters.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Ol Pejeta Conservancy (approx. 1-hour charter flight or luxury road transfer). Morning Ol Pejeta Conservancy Chimpanzee Sanctuary Visit — explore East Africa's largest black rhino sanctuary and meet the resident chimpanzees rescued from across Central Africa. Guided sanctuary tour with conservation education briefing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive across Ol Pejeta's vast plains — home to the Big Five, Grevy's zebras, and critically endangered black rhinos. Visit the memorial of Sudan, the last male northern white rhino. Participate in a private conservation briefing with a Ol Pejeta wildlife ranger about ongoing rhino protection programs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Maasai Mara lodge. Enjoy a private bonfire dinner on the lodge's exclusive bush terrace with a dedicated butler and chef, featuring a personalized menu of your preferred dishes from the week.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast: avocado and egg flatbreads, fresh juices, granola with local honey, and specialty tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ol Pejeta's premium lodge restaurant: grilled chicken, roasted sweet potatoes, garden salad, and fresh watermelon juice
meals.dinner: Private bonfire bush dinner: personalized three-course menu of guest's choice, premium wine selection, and artisan Kenyan chocolate truffles

day_by_day.notes: Chimpanzee visits at Ol Pejeta require advance booking and are limited to small groups. Photography is permitted but flash photography is prohibited near the chimps. Conservation donation included in the experience fee.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Kakamega Rainforest (approx. 1.5-hour charter flight to Kisumu, then road transfer). Morning Kakamega Rainforest Nature Walk & Birdwatching — trek through Kenya's only tropical rainforest with an expert naturalist guide. Spot rare primates including black-and-white colobus monkeys, De Brazza's monkeys, and over 330 bird species including the rare Great Blue Turaco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the rainforest exploration with a guided afternoon birdwatching session targeting endemic and rare species. Visit the forest canopy walkway for elevated views of the rainforest. Learn about the forest's unique flora, medicinal plants, and its ecological significance as an isolated Central African rainforest fragment.
day_by_day.evening: Return charter flight to Maasai Mara. Lodge spa evening — enjoy a 90-minute signature Mara massage using locally sourced botanical oils. Dinner at the lodge's fine dining restaurant with a focus on Kenyan coastal Swahili cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast before departure: fresh tropical fruits, yogurt parfait, eggs benedict, and freshly squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Rainforest picnic lunch prepared by lodge: smoked chicken wraps, local fruits, energy bars, and herbal teas
meals.dinner: Swahili coastal dinner at lodge: lobster with coconut and tamarind sauce, pilau rice, kachumbari salad, and a mango and cardamom mousse

day_by_day.notes: Kakamega is significantly more humid than the Mara — pack light breathable clothing, insect repellent, and waterproof layers. Rubber-soled trekking shoes are essential. The Great Blue Turaco is best spotted in the early morning canopy.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day in the Maasai Mara. Dedicated morning private game drive for final wildlife photography opportunities — focus on capturing the Big Five, migration herds, and predator activity with guidance from your personal photographer-guide. Sunrise drive departing at 05:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to lodge by midday for a leisurely luxury afternoon — enjoy the lodge pool, read on your private veranda, or book a final spa treatment. Optional: private guided birding walk around the lodge grounds to spot over 50 resident bird species. Pack and prepare for tomorrow's departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at the lodge — a special celebration of the journey featuring a chef's tasting menu with paired cocktails, live Maasai music, and a personalized photo book of your safari highlights presented by the lodge team as a farewell gift.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast before the game drive: granola, fresh fruit, boiled eggs, and thermos of Kenyan coffee
meals.lunch: Leisurely lodge lunch: grilled sea bass, roasted asparagus, lemon butter sauce, and a glass of chilled Sauvignon Blanc
meals.dinner: Farewell gala tasting menu: seven courses including oysters with Kilimanjaro ice melt, Mara-spiced venison, black truffle pasta, and a signature Kenyan tea-smoked dessert — paired with premium South African wines

day_by_day.notes: Request the lodge photography team to compile a digital and printed photo album of your stay — this is a premium service typically offered by luxury Mara properties. Settle any outstanding lodge bills and confirm tomorrow's transfer arrangements with the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise on the Maasai Mara — wake early for a last cup of Kenyan coffee on your private veranda watching the savannah come alive. Optional final short game drive en route to the airstrip if time permits. Private luxury transfer to Wilson Airport or JKIA Nairobi via charter flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Nairobi with time for a premium city experience: visit the Giraffe Centre to hand-feed endangered Rothschild's giraffes, or browse the Kazuri Beads workshop and Utamaduni Craft Centre for luxury Kenyan souvenirs and artisan gifts. Check into a luxury Nairobi hotel day room for freshening up before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Jomo Kenyatta International Airport. Pre-departure dinner at the Nairobi Serena Hotel's Mandhari Restaurant or the Villa Rosa Kempinski's Lucca Restaurant — both offering world-class fine dining as a perfect finale to a transformative Kenyan journey.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast: full buffet spread — fresh Mara honey, tropical fruits, eggs cooked to order, Kenyan pastries, and farewell Kenyan AA coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Nairobi's Talisman Restaurant or Carnivore Restaurant: artisan salads, grilled meats, and fresh Kenyan juices
meals.dinner: Farewell fine dining at Villa Rosa Kempinski Nairobi or Serena Hotel: contemporary European-African fusion cuisine, premium wine list, and a classic Kenyan dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at JKIA at least 3 hours before international departure. Confirm duty-free allowances for Kenyan coffee, teas, and crafts. The lodge concierge can arrange a personal shopper for last-minute luxury Kenyan souvenirs. Keep wildlife and plant products within legal export limits — no live plants, raw hides, or ivory.
